interface.title: Countess
interface.field: Plant pathology / nematology (root-knot nematode egg quantification for plant breeding)
interface.stage_of_work: Image analysis and quantification after slide preparation and imaging
interface.what_it_is_for: Counts nematode eggs in a batch of counting-slide microscope images with a trained CNN, shows an annotated preview of each slide, and exports per-image counts as a CSV.

data.note: microtiter-plate.jpg and coins.png were given together as the 'folder' through the visible multi-file input on the Count Eggs tab. They are not nematode slides. microtiter-plate.jpg got a numeric count (0) and an annotated preview with a black rectangle near the lower edge, which is the detected counting frame, not an egg detection. coins.png came back as count='error' and its preview has no annotation. Batches of two files worked. Batches of one file greyed out the page (session disconnected) every time this was tried. The About tab (screens/002.webp) lists accepted formats .jpg/.jpeg/.png/.bmp and says Download gives image_name/count pairs. Its 'Using Countess' text was written for this test deployment, is not in the repo, and says boxes are drawn around eggs, which the code contradicts. It is therefore kept as a note, not as a work step. Observed quirk: re-choosing the exact same two files in the same session ran the batch again (screens/015.webp), but the next download still had 2 data rows. The code appends results (count_eggs.py:102) and never resets them, so this is most likely because identical Shiny input values did not re-fire the counting. It is not evidence that a new batch replaces earlier results.

features.name: Batch image queue with per-item progress toasts
features.general: Choose many image files at once; the tool works through them one at a time and shows an 'item N of M' progress notice for each
features.specific: Choose Files (multiple, image/*) starts handleFileSelection → loadCurrentImage → nextImage. 'Processing image N of 2 – Analyzing image for egg counts…' toasts with a progress bar stack in the lower right. Per the code, files over 12 MB are swapped for a black placeholder (utils.py:35). Single-file batches crash (see not_done).
steps: Choose several image files in one go
Processing starts on its own; one progress toast appears per image with 'N of M' and a bar
The queue moves to the next image until all are done
serves_tasks: Load a set of images as one batch and start processing
Watch progress through the batch without stepping in

features.name: Annotated detection preview with counting-frame overlay
features.general: Show each processed image with its file name, the count written on it, an outline of the region that was counted, and outlines around detected objects, so a person can check the automatic result by eye
features.specific: The preview under Choose Files shows the image name and 'Egg count: N' drawn on the image. It also shows a black rectangle around the slide's detected counting frame (getBorders(), egg_counter.py:243); only that region is counted. Per the code, detected eggs are outlined with green contours (egg_counter.py:244), but none were seen in this run. An image whose frame cannot be found (coins.png) is shown plain, with no count, frame or contours.

serves_tasks: Visually check the counted region and the count on each image

features.name: Per-image results CSV export with error flag
features.general: Collect one result row per input file, marking files that could not be analysed as 'error' instead of dropping them, and download the table as CSV
features.specific: 'Download .csv of counts' gives counts.csv with image_name,count columns. Failed images have count='error'. Before any batch the file has only the header. Rows follow the order in which images were processed, which is the natural file-name sort applied in handleFileSelection. Results build up within a session: each processed image is appended (count_eggs.py:102) and nothing resets the table. Evidence is the downloaded text 'image_name,count\ncoins.png,error\nmicrotiter-plate.jpg,0'; no kept screen shows the CSV.
steps: Open counts.csv: one row per image, numeric count or 'error'
serves_tasks: Export per-image counts as a table
Confirm that an image that cannot be analysed is flagged rather than skipped

screens_never_reached: 'Processing Complete!' completion banner: never seen after any of the two-file batches. Screenshots taken right after the last image finished show only the final preview (screens/006.webp, screens/013.webp, screens/016.webp). Per the code it cannot appear: the observer in utils.py:88 only calls nextImage() while index < length-1, so show_completion is never set.
A preview with real egg detections (green egg contours and a count above 0): the test images are not nematode slides, so the only count was 0
not_done: Counting a single image is a limit of the tool, not just a failed attempt. Picking only one file (coins.png, or microtiter-plate.jpg, each in a fresh session) greyed out the page with an empty 'message' toast every time, which looks like a server disconnect (screens/008.webp). A reload was needed. The likely cause is ui.Progress(min=1, max=1) at count_eggs.py:82. Only two-file batches finished.
Confirming completion of an unattended batch: the progress toasts appeared, but no completion banner. This is an app bug (utils.py:88 never sets show_completion), not a missed step.
Dismissing a progress toast with ×: it was clicked, but the toasts may have closed by themselves when processing finished, so dismissing could not be confirmed.

The original 'Select Directory' button (window.showDirectoryPicker) was not used. It opens a native OS dialog that browser automation cannot fill, so the replacement multi-file input was used instead.
Checking biological accuracy of the counts: no real counting-slide images were available among the test files.
